topic: He must have missed the bus
title: He must have missed the bus
pt: Foco da aula: must have + particípio: dedução sobre o passado

solo90.name: Pausa

lines.en: Dan, the bus is twenty minutes late again. It must have broken down somewhere on the high street.
lines.pt: Dan, o ônibus está vinte minutos atrasado de novo. Deve ter quebrado em algum ponto da rua principal.

lines.en: Or the driver must have picked another route because of the roadworks. They closed half the road yesterday.
lines.pt: Ou o motorista deve ter escolhido outro caminho por causa das obras. Fecharam metade da rua ontem.

lines.en: That would explain the crowd. Everybody here must have been waiting since eight, judging by their faces.
lines.pt: Isso explicaria a multidão. Todo mundo aqui deve estar esperando desde as oito, pelo que mostram os rostos.

lines.en: Look at that woman with the suitcase. She must have missed her train because of this delay.
lines.pt: Olhe aquela mulher com a mala. Ela deve ter perdido o trem por causa desse atraso.

lines.en: Poor thing. And where is Mark? He must have overslept, because he never misses the early bus.
lines.pt: Coitada. E onde está o Mark? Ele deve ter dormido demais, porque nunca perde o ônibus cedo.

lines.en: He must have caught an earlier one. He told me yesterday that he had to be at the office before the meeting.
lines.pt: Ele deve ter pegado um mais cedo. Ontem ele me disse que tinha de estar no escritório antes da reunião.

lines.en: Then he must have been very lucky. His phone is off, so he must have let it die again.
lines.pt: Então ele deve ter tido muita sorte. O celular dele está desligado, então deve ter esquecido de carregar de novo.

lines.en: That sounds like Mark. He must have run out of battery on the way, as usual.
lines.pt: Isso é a cara do Mark. Ele deve ter ficado sem bateria no caminho, como sempre.

lines.en: Look, a replacement bus is coming round the corner. Someone must have phoned the company after all.
lines.pt: Olhe, um ônibus de substituição está vindo na esquina. Alguém deve ter ligado para a empresa, afinal.

lines.en: Finally! The passengers must have complained loudly enough. Let’s get on before the whole crowd pushes in.
lines.pt: Finalmente! Os passageiros devem ter reclamado alto o bastante. Vamos entrar antes que a multidão toda empurre.

lines.en: Good idea. I hope Mark hasn’t walked all the way. He must have been exhausted.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Espero que o Mark não tenha ido a pé o caminho todo. Ele deve ter ficado exausto.

items.fix: He must have missed the bus.
items.why: Use must have + participle for deductions about the past.

items.wrong: She must have forgot her keys.

facts.label: Deduções sobre o passado
facts.sub: Quando você quase tem certeza: He must have missed the bus. Evidência no presente, conclusão sobre o passado. Sem to e sempre com o particípio.

facts.label: Deve ter
facts.sub: Use must have + particípio quando você tem quase certeza de algo no passado, a partir de evidências: The road is wet, so it must have rained. É a dedução mais forte sobre o passado.

facts.label: Verbos irregulares
facts.sub: Aprenda os particípios dos verbos mais úteis para deduzir: been, gone, taken, forgotten, broken, missed, caught. Sem o particípio certo a frase fica errada.

facts.label: Must have

facts.label: Sem to

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Must have + participle expresses a strong deduction about the past.
items.why: Yes.

items.s: “He must have left” means he may leave tomorrow.
items.why: It is about the past.
We need the participle: forgotten.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Must have + participle expresses a strong deduction about the past. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
“He must have left” means he may leave tomorrow. → Falso (It is about the past.)
We say “She must have forgot”. → Falso (We need the participle: forgotten.)

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 2/2

items.s: Must have is used when we are almost certain.
items.why: Yes.

items.s: The negative deduction uses can’t have.
items.why: Yes, but that is another lesson.

pages.title: A late bus in London · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a grey Tuesday in London, and the rush hour has started. Dozens of people wait at the bus stop with umbrellas. Beth knows the timetable of her commute by heart. Today nothing runs on time. Her colleague Dan arrives and looks at the empty road. They try to work out what went wrong.

“Dan, the bus is twenty minutes late again. It must have broken down somewhere on the high street.” says Beth. “Or the driver must have picked another route because of the roadworks. They closed half the road yesterday.” says Dan. “That would explain the crowd. Everybody here must have been waiting since eight, judging by their faces.” says Beth.
